transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, Astra Labs), Rosa Nguyen (Platform Lead), Tomás Alvarez (Security)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check-in to align on EU dedicated nodes, throughput targets, and contract term. Confirmed timeline for SOW and benchmark run. Security questions around key management and data residency flagged for follow-up.

Topics: renewal term, capacity bump (EU), VPC/KMS integration, latency vs cost tradeoffs, pilot benchmark schedule, pricing cadence

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick intro from our side, Samir and I — Maya from account, Samir is our solutions eng, he'll run the benchmark and the config.
[00:18] Jordan: Cool, thanks. Quick context from us: we've been on Redwood for 9 months, using the hosted tier for inference, but now traffic is up and we need EU locality and more predictable throughput. We're looking at 12 month term with a committed baseline.
[00:34] Rosa: Yep, our main constraints are P95 latency <180ms for single-turn generation at 1k tokens and region-specific data residency for EU customers. Also security wants KMS or customer-managed keys.
[00:52] Samir: Right, okay. So two things: dedicated capacity in EU and key mgmt — on the dedicated side we can reserve GPU pools and configure autoscale/burst. There is a tradeoff: lower unit cost with bigger reserved pools but you pay for idle.
[01:05] Tomás: Can you walk me through the KMS flow? We need to ensure those keys never leave our control.
[01:18] Samir: Absolutely. We support customer KMS integration — you bring your key in KMS or HSM, Redwood's control plane stores a wrapped key and the inference plane in the VPC uses a transient unwrap with limited lifetime. The audit logs show key usage. Note: in some transcripts KMS is transcribed as K-MS, sorry for that.
[01:40] Jordan: And what about private deployment? We had internal discussions around self-hosting vs Redwood private.
[01:48] Maya: We talked about that in the last week — Private deployment is available but usually overkill unless you need full air-gap or on-prem. Most customers prefer Dedicated+VPC because you get isolation and managed ops.
[02:05] Rosa: For our compliance team, SOC 2 and ISO certs are a must. Do you have the docs?
[02:12] Maya: Yes, we'll send the SOC 2 report and the compliance pack. Also include the network diagram for EU onramp.
[02:20] Tomás: Can we get specifics on RBAC and SSO? We use SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning.
[02:27] Samir: We support SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC. We'll share the SAML attribute map and recommended roles. Small caveat: role propagation to the private nodes depends on the VPC peering timing — we'll call that out in the SOW.
[02:45] Jordan: On numbers, our current peak is ~250 RPS for short chat flows, average seq length 220 tokens, but we have spikes to 1.1k RPS for batch scoring. We need predictability for Black Friday-like events in Q4.
[03:05] Rosa: Also want to understand cache behavior — prefix caching was improving latency for us but we saw cache churn when model variants flip.
[03:14] Samir: Good note. We have auto-prefix and KV cache controls. For a multi-model rollout you can pin versions and use canary routing so cache warmup is controlled. That reduces cold-start token cost.
[03:35] Maya: Price discussion — to keep ARR predictable, we can do a committed baseline for 12 months with tiered pricing for burst. Example numbers we'll formalize in the SOW.
[03:48] Jordan: What's the path if we need to lower latency further? Quantization or smaller model copy?
[03:55] Samir: Options: quantized snapshots (we support int8/4), more aggressive batching controls, and local EU edge nodes to cut egress. There is a small hit in output fidelity with aggressive quantization — recommend running eval sets.
[04:15] Tomás: Are there known regressions with quantized models? We can't accept user-facing hallucination increases.
[04:22] Samir: We'll tie quantization to your eval harness — Redwood Optimize can run quality checks against your prompt set and alert on regressions. We'll include that in the pilot.
[05:00] Jordan: Timeline-wise we need EU nodes live before 2026-11-01. Is that feasible?
[05:07] Maya: Yes, if we sign SOW mid-September we can stage nodes in October and run a commissioning plan. That's tight but doable.
[05:18] Rosa: Ok — what does the benchmark look like?
[05:22] Samir: 24h steady-state run simulating 1M tokens/day with production seq distribution. We'll validate P50/P95/P99 latencies and token cost. We'll also run a burst test for 2x peak for 30 minutes.
[05:35] Jordan: Will the benchmark use our hidden data? We need to ensure token logs aren't retained beyond the run.
[05:42] Samir: We'll set ephemeral logging and ensure logs are deleted after results are packaged, and we can sign a bench NDA.
[06:00] Maya: Quick check — pricing/contract term: are you leaning to a 12 or 24 month?
[06:07] Jordan: 12 month to start with option to renew/extend at 9 months. Budget cycle prefers annual.
[06:14] Rosa: Also want EU-only residency for EU production traffic — can we route EU-traffic to EU nodes only?
[06:20] Samir: Yes, smart routing supports region pinning by route or token. We can also set fallback policies to US if EU capacity is exhausted but that'll be a contractual decision — many customers opt for strict residency (no fallback) or soft fallback for SLAs.
[06:40] Tomás: Any competitors we should be worried about? Our infra team mentioned FastServe and in-house options.
[06:46] Maya: FastServe is usually cheaper at first but lacks our Optimize tooling and observability at token-level. Self-host is flexible but ops burden is high.
[07:05] Rosa: Ops question — how are upgrades handled? Kernel/serving runtime patches?
[07:12] Samir: For Dedicated we do controlled rollouts, canary nodes first, and we provide rollout windows. For Private you'd control patching cadence.
[07:30] Jordan: Re: billing, we need invoice-level details for cost center mapping.
[07:35] Maya: We'll provide line item invoices with committed units, burst usage, and data transfer. We'll also add a billing contact.
[07:48] Rosa: Anything else on security? Data encryption at rest, in transit?
[07:52] Samir: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.3 in flight. We support customer-managed keys for both.
[08:05] (brief cross talk about internal calendar conflicts)
[08:18] Jordan: Let's outline next steps — we need SOW and pricing, compliance pack, and benchmark schedule.
[08:24] Maya: Confirming: Maya to draft SOW; Samir to provision bench cluster; Rosa to share telemetry; Tomás will review KMS and compliance details.
[08:35] Tomás: I'll need the KMS flow doc and a sample audit log schema.
[08:42] Samir: I'll attach an example audit log and the KMS integration doc in the follow-up.
[08:50] Jordan: Good. Any blockers from our side?
[08:54] Rosa: Nothing immediate — timeline dependent on internal budget sign-off but we're optimistic.
[09:01] Maya: Great. We'll target SOW sent by 2026-09-03 and bench week of 2026-09-06.
[09:10] (wrap)
[09:12] Maya: Thanks everyone, I'll follow up with the artifacts.
[09:15] Jordan: Appreciate it.
[09:20] END

Call notes: this transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and some speaker label noise (speaker turns merged). See metadata for action items and next steps.
